matches.rationale: GT#1 describes cherry-picking and omission of negative results in Section 4.1 performance tables, leading to inflated metrics with low variance. Finding #7 directly identifies the same issue: Section 4.1 discloses exclusion of baselines and negative cases where ConML fails, post-hoc hyperparameter optimization, and optimistic variance from excluding fluctuating runs.

GT#2 points to inconsistent/vague specification of the projection function ψ across meta-learners (especially ICL) in Section 3.1 and 3.3. Finding #2 identifies that the per-task inner-task distance d_τ^{in} referenced as equation (1) is never actually defined anywhere in the paper, blocking reproducibility of how representations are computed—the same underlying issue of incomplete method specification.

GT#3 concerns unfair experimental protocol: reusing meta-training hyperparameters at meta-test without tuning baselines, and omitting computational cost profiling during meta-testing. None of the findings address meta-test hyperparameter reuse, baseline tuning fairness, or meta-test computational profiling.

GT#4 identifies overstated claims in the Abstract about 'seamless integration' and 'significant boost with small implementation cost' relative to limited experimental scope. Finding #7 addresses selective reporting but not the overstatement of integration ease or implementation cost claims in the Abstract.

GT#5 concerns omission of ethical considerations (environmental impact, energy, fairness, bias) in the Discussion section. None of the findings mention ethical integrity, environmental impact, or responsible AI considerations.

GT#6 identifies overly strong theoretical claims in Lemma 1 and Theorem 1 (Section 3.2) with missing assumptions and unproven statements. Findings #1, #3, #5 all identify mathematical errors in the Appendix B proofs (false equivalences, incorrect bounds, unsubstantiated steps), and Finding #6 confirms the claimed generalization guarantee does not follow from the proof—all addressing the same theoretical validity issue.

GT#7 describes selective reporting in Section 4.3 (Tables 4, hyperparameter ablations) showing only partial results without variance or failure modes. Finding #7 identifies the same selective reporting practice disclosed in Section 4.1, which applies to the experimental results throughout including the ablation studies.

GT#8 concerns the mismatch between the Abstract's claim of full problem- and learner-agnosticism versus the Method's dependence on episodic mini-batch framework and task identity. None of the findings address this specific scope limitation or the incoherence between claimed generality and actual framework requirements.

GT#9 identifies mischaracterization of prior work in the Related Work section, claiming no counterpart exists while selectively citing and misrepresenting prior contrastive meta-learning approaches. None of the findings address citation practices or related work misrepresentation.

GT#10 concerns overly promotional language in the Conclusion (Section 6) without sufficient caveats. While Finding #7 addresses Abstract vs Results mismatch, none of the findings specifically identify rhetorical overstatement in the Conclusion section.

GT#11 identifies vague specification of the inner-task distance computation in Section 3.1, particularly the sampling strategy π_κ and subset properties. Finding #2 directly identifies that the inner-task distance d_τ^{in} computation is never defined (missing equation 1), which is the same reproducibility issue.

GT#12 concerns the mismatch between claims about applicability to real-world pretrained LLMs (Abstract/Introduction) versus experiments only on synthetic tasks with GPT-2 trained from scratch (Section 4.4). None of the findings address this specific ICL generalization claim vs evidence gap.

GT#13 identifies confounding from simultaneous changes in backbone architecture and ConML integration, preventing isolation of ConML's effect. None of the findings address architectural confounds or ablation control issues.

GT#14 concerns overstated interpretation of ablation results in Section 4.3.2 and Figure 2 (λ sensitivity, distance metrics), glossing over model collapse and fragility. While Finding #7 addresses selective reporting broadly, it does not specifically identify the mischaracterization of sensitivity/robustness results in the ablation studies.

GT#15 identifies lack of statistical significance testing, confidence intervals, and reporting of random seeds/trials across experimental tables. None of the findings address missing statistical rigor or significance testing in the reported results.
